samples.summary: New `YorkieDocStore.dispose()` (unsubscribe + clear `onRemoteChange`) has no test at all
samples.evidence: `dispose()` is the whole point of this delta — it stops a replaced store from continuing to handle `remote-change` and driving a disposed editor. I grepped the frontend suite for `dispose` / `unsubscribe` / `onRemoteChange` / `remote-change` in `packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts`: the only hit is line 1863, a comment where the test *simulates* a remote change by poking the private `store.dirty` / `store.cachedDoc` fields, i.e. the subscription callback path is never exercised. No test asserts (a) `onRemoteChange` is not invoked after `dispose()`, (b) `dispose()` is idempotent (documented as such in the new JSDoc), or (c) the doc subscription is actually released. The suite already constructs a real `yorkie.Document` in `beforeEach`, and `packages/frontend/tests/app/files/pdf-collab.test.tsx:95` shows the same store-dispose pattern is testable here. If `dispose()` silently fails to unsubscribe, the regression it fixes (stale store publishing presence into a disposed editor) ships back undetected and nothing in the suite goes red.

samples.summary: No test covers the docs-view cleanup calling `store.dispose()` on editor teardown / `readOnly` change
samples.evidence: The effect cleanup now calls `store.dispose()` before nulling `storeRef`, and the comment claims the `editor`→`viewer` downgrade rebuild is the motivating path. There is no test file for `docs-view.tsx` (only `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/image-insert.test.ts` exists under src/app/docs, and `packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/` contains only store/editor-level tests). So nothing asserts that on a `readOnly` flip the old store stops receiving `remote-change`, nor that ordering (dispose before `storeRef.current = null`) is preserved. A future reorder or removal of this line re-introduces a stale store publishing presence into a disposed editor with no failing test.

samples.summary: Share-link revalidation (periodic re-resolve, retry:1 eviction, downgrade to viewer) is untested
samples.evidence: `SharedDocumentByToken` was rewritten from a one-shot `useEffect` fetch to a polling `useQuery` with `refetchInterval: SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS`, `staleTime: 0`, `retry: 1`. The stated behaviors — a revoked link eventually closes the view, an `editor`→`viewer` downgrade tightens `readOnly`, and a single blip does not evict the session — have no coverage. The only test touching this file is `packages/frontend/src/app/shared/__tests__/shared-blob-routing.test.ts`, which only exercises the pure `sharedBlobKind` helper; grepping `packages/frontend/tests` for `refetchInterval`/`useQuery` returns nothing, and no test references `SharedDocumentByToken`. `packages/frontend/src/app/templates/template-review-queue.test.tsx` shows react-query component tests are feasible in this repo. If the revalidation silently stops working, a revoked/downgraded link keeps its authority for the tab's lifetime — the exact regression this change exists to prevent — with a green suite.

samples.summary: Rewritten error/empty-token rendering branch has no test
samples.evidence: The error path was restructured: loading is now gated on `token && isLoading`, and the message is derived inline (`!token` → "No share token provided", else `error instanceof Error && error.message` → fallback "Invalid or expired link"). With `enabled: false` for a missing token, react-query's `isLoading` semantics decide whether a tokenless mount shows a spinner forever or the error card. Nothing tests either branch — no test renders `SharedDocumentByToken` (see searches). Failure mode is a visible but contained UI regression (blank/stuck screen instead of "Link unavailable").
searchedFor: Grep 'Link unavailable|No share token provided' across packages/frontend

verdict.reason: Verified independently: `YorkieDocStore.dispose()` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:651-655) releases the `doc.subscribe` handle set at line 633 and clears `onRemoteChange` (invoked at line 636), and is called in production only from docs-view.tsx:574 during editor rebuild/cleanup. No test anywhere exercises it. I grepped `dispose` across all test/spec/integration files repo-wide: the only frontend store-dispose hits are packages/frontend/tests/app/files/pdf-collab.test.tsx:95 and :267, which dispose a PdfCommentStore (constructed at line 89), a different class. I enumerated every `new YorkieDocStore(...)` construction site (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts, merge-repro.test.ts:55, editor-undo-selection.test.ts:118, editor-step-selection-font-size-undo.test.ts:90, tests/helpers/two-user-docs-yorkie.ts:111,137) — none call dispose(). `onRemoteChange` appears in tests only for the slides store (tests/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.test.ts:426-436). The docs suite's single `remote-change` reference (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:1863) is a comment above a manual poke of private `dirty`/`cachedDoc`, so the subscription callback path is never driven. There is no DocsView-level or e2e test covering the cleanup indirectly. So nothing asserts (a) onRemoteChange is not invoked after dispose, (b) idempotency documented in the JSDoc, or (c) that the subscription is actually released. The gap is testable in-repo: src/app/board/yorkie-board-store.test.ts:16,320 synthesizes `remote-change` events for the analogous board store. Major under this lens: the untested behavior is the whole delta, and its failure lets a stale store keep refreshing/publishing presence into a disposed editor — a user-visible regression that would ship green.

No test file anywhere imports `docs-view` or `docs-detail` — the only importers are production files (docs-detail.tsx:27, shared-document.tsx:34, docs-export-button.tsx:16 type-only).
